anti_overlap: Focus is on gate model correctness, procedure entry/exit formality, and emergency exit availability — not keymap palette ergonomics (DAW domain), not selection enum variant completeness (broadcast domain), not event propagation/click-through (stage management domain), not kitchen ticket state collision (restaurant domain)
decision_lens: Does the input system's gate model provide the same quality of protection as a formal nuclear procedure — clearly delineating what actions are permissible in each modal state, with no ambiguity about which gate applies to which input, and with a formal entry/exit path for each modal boundary?
distance_rationale: Nuclear control room procedure discipline has the most formally specified action-gate model outside of aviation — their two-tier distinction between surveillance and action procedures, two-person integrity for destructive actions, concurrent procedure prohibition, and emergency procedure preemption map with exactness onto the two-predicate gate model, Ctrl+Q guard, direct-switch atomicity, and Esc stack model.
expected_isomorphisms: Action procedure entry → Esc opens pause menu. Surveillance procedure → screen overlay (camera live). Action procedure → pause menu (camera frozen). Two-person integrity → Ctrl+Q modifier guard or two-step confirm. Concurrent procedure prohibition → direct-switch atomic close-then-open. Emergency procedure preemption → Esc-always-opens-pause-menu. Procedure applicability display → HUD legend active chip.
focus: Procedure binder engagement protocol, action gate discipline, two-person integrity rules, and modal procedure state in nuclear control room operations
name: fd-nuclear-procedure-binder-gate-model
persona: Apply the perspective of a licensed reactor operator and procedure writer with experience in pressurized water reactor control rooms — they care about the strict distinction between surveillance procedures (observation only, no system changes) and action procedures (licensed to manipulate), the two-person integrity requirement for destructive actions, and the formal procedure entry/exit protocol that governs what other tasks are permissible while a procedure is open.
review_areas: Procedure entry/exit formality: in nuclear operations, entering a procedure requires explicit acknowledgment — the pause menu open (Esc) and close (backtick or Esc again) sequence is this entry/exit protocol; verify that the procedure entry (Esc opens pause menu) cannot be triggered accidentally while the player is performing another action, and that exit (backtick) always restores the prior state cleanly

Action gate vs. surveillance gate distinction: reactor operators distinguish procedures that permit manipulation from those that permit only observation — is_pause_menu() gates manipulation (camera, Space, speed); is_input_modal() gates even observation-adjacent actions (picking, Tab); review whether this two-tier distinction is expressed in code as two distinct SystemSet gates or collapsed into one

Two-person integrity for destructive actions: nuclear regulations require two licensed operators for irreversible manipulations — Ctrl+Q is the renderer equivalent; verify that Quit requires either a two-step confirmation (pause menu → Quit button) or a modifier key guard, and that this guard is not also gated by is_input_modal() in a way that would prevent the emergency exit from firing

Concurrent procedure prohibition: nuclear ops forbid opening a second action procedure while one is already in progress — the digit-direct-switch closes the current overlay before opening the new one; verify that this atomic swap is implemented correctly and that no frame exists where two overlays are simultaneously active

Procedure applicability check: before a procedure can be executed, the operator verifies it is applicable to the current plant state — the HUD legend strip is the renderer analog; verify that the active overlay's chip highlights immediately on open, so the player always knows which procedure is currently active

Abnormal procedure preemption: emergency procedures can preempt normal ones — the Esc-always-opens-pause-menu (even when an overlay is open) is this preemption path; verify that the pause menu stack model correctly captures the screen overlay state so that closing the pause menu restores the prior procedure (overlay), not a blank state

severity_examples.condition: Esc is handled by two independent systems without declared ordering; the quit-on-escape system does not check pause_menu: true as an early-return before checking is_input_modal()
severity_examples.scenario: Esc pressed while an overlay is open fires both the pause menu open handler AND the quit-on-escape handler in the same frame — the quit handler is gated by is_input_modal() but the pause menu open has already written pause_menu: true before the quit handler checks, causing indeterminate ordering

severity_examples.condition: Emergency exit (Ctrl+Q) accidentally added to the GatedInput system set alongside Space and picking; should only be gated by a modifier-key requirement, not by overlay state
severity_examples.scenario: Ctrl+Q is gated by is_input_modal() to prevent accidental quit from within an overlay — but this also prevents the emergency exit from firing when the player is stuck in an unrecoverable overlay state, defeating its purpose as an always-available escape

severity_examples.condition: HUD legend update system runs in a different stage from OverlayState write, causing one-frame visual desync
severity_examples.scenario: The HUD legend strip chip highlight does not update within the same frame that an overlay opens — for one frame the player sees the legend with no active chip, then it pops on — the active procedure display lags behind actual state

source_domain: Nuclear reactor control room procedure binder protocol and licensed operator gate discipline
success_hints: Verify that Ctrl+Q is NOT in the GatedInput SystemSet — it should be gated only by a modifier key, never by overlay modal state

Check that the quit-on-escape handler (Esc → quit when no overlay) and the pause-menu open handler (Esc → open pause menu) are mutually exclusive and ordering-declared — they must not both fire in the same frame
Confirm that direct-switch (digit-N while overlay-M is open) closes M and opens N in a single system with no intermediate state where both are active
Verify that HUD legend chip highlight update is in the same system or stage as the OverlayState write that opens/closes overlays
task_context: Reviewing the two-predicate gate model (is_pause_menu vs is_input_modal), Esc semantics stack model, direct overlay switching, HUD legend active state, and Ctrl+Q emergency exit for a Bevy 0.18 native renderer input system.
